title: Membranolytic peptide programs immunogenic cell death for cancer therapy.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and opened every publicly reachable file: Supplementary Information PDF (23 MB, text extracted, 98,630 characters), Supplementary Table xlsx (12 KB) and the Supplementary Source Data zip (140 KB). The zip holds exactly 6 Excel files (157 KB total) of mouse tumour volume curves and organ imaging intensities; the largest sheet is 67 rows by 42 columns. The xlsx is a single list of 128 mouse gene symbols (an interferon-stimulated-gene signature), nothing else. I also checked NCBI GEO (gene expression archive), SRA (sequence read archive), BioProject, Europe PMC text-mined accessions, PubMed cross-links and Zenodo for a deposited dataset: all returned nothing for this paper.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That bulk RNA sequencing (n = 3 mice per group) and single-cell RNA sequencing of CD45-positive immune cells were performed; the Methods describe them but no accession number or data availability statement appears anywhere in the Supplementary Information, and the main article text is paywalled so I could not read its Data availability section. The list of 10 peptide variants (MPC16, aMPC16-DA50, -TA50, -CA30, -CA50, -CA70, -AA50, aMPC12-CA50, aMPC6-CA50, iMP) comes from the Methods text, not from a table of sequences.

a1_downloadable.note: The figure source data downloads fine (I opened it), but the only substantial dataset in the paper - bulk RNA sequencing and single-cell RNA sequencing - has no accession number in GEO, SRA, BioProject, Europe PMC or Zenodo, and none is stated in the Supplementary Information. The main article is paywalled, so its data availability statement is unreadable. Effectively 'not locatable'.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No prediction target column exists. The files hold only tumour volume over time per mouse and organ fluorescence intensity. Any machine-learning label (for example membrane-rupturing potency per peptide) would have to be reconstructed by reading numbers off figure panels.

a3_inputs_present.note: The membranolytic agents are random poly(amino acid) copolymers named by composition (for example aMPC16-CA50 = 50% citraconic-acid modification), not defined amino acid sequences. No sequence or chemical structure string is given anywhere in the files, so there is nothing a sequence or molecule model could read.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are stated in the sheet headers I opened: tumour volume in cubic millimetres, dose in micrograms, average radiant efficiency for imaging.

a5_enough_rows.note: Verified in the files: 6 source-data spreadsheets totalling 157 KB; the biggest single sheet is 67 timepoints by 42 mice. The modelling unit would be the peptide variant, and there are 10 of them. The checklist needs about 1,500 labelled rows, or 400 for classification.

a6_fits_laptop.note: 157 KB of spreadsheets plus a 23 MB PDF. Trivially fits; this is the only Part A item that is comfortably passed.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: The per-mouse group sizes in the sheets I opened are consistent with the figure legends in the Supplementary Information (for example n = 3 mice for the RNA sequencing arm).

a8_label_provenance.note: There is no label to trace. The nearest measured quantities (tumour volume, dye leakage from liposomes) are real physical measurements, but they are reported per experimental group in figures rather than as a label column, so provenance cannot be checked at row level.

existing_models.name: In silico design and optimization of selective membranolytic anticancer peptides (Scientific Reports 2019, support vector machine / gradient boosting / random forest classifiers)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported 83% of 12 computationally designed peptides correct on wet-lab validation; train/test split details not retrieved beyond the abstract.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Separating anticancer activity from toxicity to healthy cells (selectivity) across design-synthesize-test cycles.

existing_models.name: HemoDL (double-ensemble hemolytic peptide predictor using sequence features plus transformer embeddings)
existing_models.score_and_split: Abstract reports benchmark datasets D1-D4 split 80/20 train/test; exact headline numbers not retrieved.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Quantitative (rather than yes/no) prediction of hemolytic concentration.

existing_models.name: HemPepPred (hemolytic activity regression on ESM2_t33 protein language model embeddings plus physicochemical descriptors)
existing_models.score_and_split: R-squared 0.57, correlation 0.76 on a held-out 20% test set (random split, per abstract).
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Generalisation of quantitative hemolysis prediction beyond the curated benchmark sets.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (a protein language model) would be the natural choice for peptide activity prediction
backbone.hardware: Not applicable - no sequences exist in this data to embed.
backbone.licence: ESM-2 is MIT licensed, but irrelevant here.

integration.partner_dataset: None usable. DBAASP (Database of Antimicrobial Activity and Structure of Peptides) and CancerPPD hold peptide activity data, but they are keyed on amino acid sequence and this paper's agents are undefined random copolymers.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written - there is no shared identifier in the downloadable files, so the join would be decoration.

controls.positive_control: None available at row level; the liposome dye-leakage assay with Triton X-100 as 100% leakage is a proper wet-lab positive control but exists only inside figures.
controls.negative_control: Not runnable - there is no model to shuffle labels for.
controls.external_validation: None - the RNA sequencing that could have been validated against public interferon-response datasets was never deposited.

honest_claim_h3: No honest machine-learning claim is possible: the downloadable data is 157 KB of mouse tumour growth curves for 10 peptide variants, with no sequence inputs, no label column, and no deposited sequencing data.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use peptide composition to predict how strongly a membrane-rupturing peptide kills tumour cells and triggers immune recognition.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would show the model each peptide variant's chemistry (hydrophobic tail length, fraction of acid-responsive modification) plus the pH it was tested at. Verified count of distinct peptide variants in this paper: 10.
plain_idea.predict: How much membrane rupture or tumour-cell killing the peptide causes, measured by dye leakage from artificial lipid vesicles and by cell-viability assays. Both are real lab measurements, but reported only inside figure panels.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Peptide chemists designing acid-responsive anticancer peptides would get a cheaper way to rank candidates before synthesis. Even a failed model would say how much of membranolytic potency is explained by bulk composition alone.

more_or_better_data.why: This paper contributes 10 peptide variants with no sequences. The existing hemolysis and anticancer-peptide models are trained on curated benchmark sets of thousands of sequences (DBAASP, CancerPPD, HemoPI-derived sets).

confidence_score.why: Replicates exist (3-8 mice per group in the sheets I opened), but per-peptide replication of the activity measurement is not in any downloadable file, so no per-prediction uncertainty could be estimated.

models_beatable.why: HemPepPred (2025) already uses ESM-2 protein language model embeddings and reports R-squared 0.57; with 10 unlabelled copolymers there is nothing to beat it with.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails the first condition: our model cannot see everything the baseline sees, because this paper supplies no amino acid sequences and no activity label column.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: predict membranolytic potency or immunogenic-cell-death capacity from peptide composition. Dead on arrival because the paper's agents are 10 undefined random copolymers rather than sequences, the activity numbers live in figure panels rather than a label column, and the bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing that would have been the real dataset was never deposited in any public archive I could find.

effort.compute_note: Measured file sizes directly: 157 KB of source-data spreadsheets plus a 23 MB PDF. No modelling estimates given because there is no feature/label table to build.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Unzip the Supplementary Source Data (140 KB) and count rows: 6 spreadsheets of mouse tumour volumes, largest sheet 67 by 42, and 10 peptide variants total. Two minutes, and it kills the project.

verdict_reason: Experimental peptide-therapy paper. Verified in the files: the only public data is 157 KB of mouse tumour growth curves and organ imaging plus a 128-gene list. Fails A1 (the bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing has no accession in GEO, SRA, BioProject or Zenodo, and the article's data availability statement is paywalled), A2 (no label column), A3 (the peptides are random copolymers with no sequences given), and A5 (10 peptide variants, versus the ~400 minimum). Hemolysis and anticancer-peptide prediction is also already served by sequence-based models including a 2025 ESM-2-based regressor.
